stem: Which of these is an application of artificial intelligence?

options.content: A phone app that identifies a plant disease from a photograph
options.rationale: Correct: image recognition is an AI application.

options.content: A word processor that counts the words in a document for the writer
options.rationale: Counting words follows a fixed rule and needs no learning.

options.content: A calculator that adds two numbers entered by the user
options.rationale: Arithmetic is not an AI application.

options.content: A printer that prints one page after another from a queue
options.rationale: Printing is not AI.

explanation: AI tasks include recognising images and speech, translating and recommending.

stem: What is the most common cause of bias in an AI system?

options.content: Training data that does not represent every group of users
options.rationale: Correct.

options.content: The computer that runs the system is too old to be fair
options.rationale: The age of the computer does not cause unfairness.

options.content: The program is written in a language that few people know
options.rationale: The programming language is not the cause.

options.content: The people who use the system type too slowly on the keys of the computer
options.rationale: User speed is not a cause.

explanation: The system learns the patterns in its data, including gaps in the data.

stem: A bank replaces some of its counter staff with a chatbot. Which statement describes an effect on employment?

options.content: No jobs at the bank are affected in any way at all
options.rationale: Some tasks have changed.

options.content: Some jobs may be lost while others are created
options.rationale: Correct: the effect is mixed.

options.content: Every job in the bank is lost once the chatbot starts
options.rationale: Not every job can be done by a chatbot.

options.content: Only the customers' jobs change, and the staff are unaffected
options.rationale: The staff's work is affected.

explanation: Automation changes tasks: it removes some jobs and creates others.

stem: Why should the accuracy of an AI system be measured separately for different groups of users, as well as overall?

options.content: Separate figures are always higher than the overall figure is
options.rationale: They can be lower or higher than the overall figure.

options.content: The law requires that a single figure is never published
options.rationale: No such rule is stated.

options.content: A single overall figure is impossible to calculate in any practical way
options.rationale: It can be calculated easily.

options.content: An overall figure can hide poor results for a smaller group of users
options.rationale: Correct.

explanation: A high overall figure can come from a large, well-served group.
hints: What happens to a small group's results when they are averaged with a large group's?

stem: A voice-controlled app needs recordings of the user's voice. Which concern does this mainly raise?

options.content: The speed at which the processor runs its programs
options.rationale: That is a performance matter.

options.content: The size of the keyboard that the user is given
options.rationale: A keyboard may not be used.

options.content: The privacy of the user's personal data
options.rationale: Correct: recordings are personal data and must be protected.

options.content: The colour that is chosen for the screen display
options.rationale: That has no link with personal data.

explanation: Recordings of a person's voice can identify them and show what they said.
hints: What kind of information is a recording of someone's voice?

stem: Which statement describes an environmental impact of AI?

options.content: AI has no environmental impact at all because it is only software
options.rationale: Computers use energy.

options.content: Training large systems uses much electricity, but AI may also reduce waste
options.rationale: Correct: both effects are possible.

options.content: AI always reduces the energy used by every industry that adopts it
options.rationale: That ignores its own energy use.

options.content: Only farmers are affected by the energy that AI systems use
options.rationale: Anyone who uses the electricity supply is affected.

explanation: Give both the energy cost and the possible benefits.
hints: Is the impact only harmful or only helpful?

stem: A clinic uses AI to suggest a diagnosis from a scan. Who should make the final decision about treatment?

options.content: The AI system alone, without any person at all checking its result
options.rationale: A system cannot be held accountable.

options.content: The software company, without ever seeing the patient
options.rationale: The patient's own clinician is best placed to decide.

options.content: A qualified health worker who is responsible for the patient
options.rationale: Correct: a person must stay accountable, especially where safety is involved.

options.content: Whoever pays for the scan to be carried out at the clinic
options.rationale: Payment does not decide medical judgements.

explanation: AI can support a decision but a person remains responsible.

stem: Which is a benefit of machine translation for African languages?

options.content: Every translation that is produced is guaranteed to be perfect in meaning
options.rationale: Accuracy is lower for languages with little data.

options.content: Human translators are never needed again for any task
options.rationale: People are still needed to check.

options.content: Languages no longer need to be taught in any school
options.rationale: Teaching remains needed.

options.content: More people can read information in the language they use daily
options.rationale: Correct.

explanation: Access improves, but quality depends on the data available.

stem: An AI system is accurate for all groups of people if it is accurate overall.
explanation: False. A good overall figure can hide poor results for a smaller group.

stem: Because an AI system makes the decision, the people who built and use it are not responsible for the results.
explanation: False. People who design, train and use the system remain responsible.

stem: Match each application of AI to an example.

right.content: Suggesting a video based on what a user watched before
Answering a customer's question in a chat window
A machine that moves parts on a production line
Typing a message by speaking to a phone
Spotting a crop disease from a photograph

explanation: Each is a common AI application.

stem: Complete the sentences about bias.

payload.template: AI bias is often caused by training {{blank:a}} that does not {{blank:b}} all groups. It can be reduced by collecting more {{blank:c}} data.

explanation: Unrepresentative data causes bias; more representative data helps.
hints: Think about why the data matters.

stem: A chatbot at a clinic is tested on 60 questions from patients who speak one language and answers 45 correctly. What is its accuracy for that group?
In the same test, the app is 90% accurate on maize and 60% accurate on sorghum. What is the difference in accuracy, in percentage points?
explanation: 30 percentage points.
workedSolution: Accuracy for maize = 135 ÷ 150 = 90%; for sorghum 30 ÷ 50 = 60%. The difference is 90 − 60 = 30 percentage points.

stem: What word describes systematic unfairness in the results of an AI system, often caused by its training data?
explanation: Bias.

stem: Describe two applications of AI, with one benefit or concern for each. [4]

points.description: A named application, for example image recognition for crop disease or speech recognition
A benefit or concern linked to it (early warning for farmers; wrong identification; privacy of recordings)
A second, different application, for example a chatbot or machine translation
A benefit or concern linked to it (24-hour service; wrong answers; less accurate for languages with little data)

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Image recognition can identify a crop disease from a photograph, giving a farmer early warning, though a wrong identification could lead to the wrong treatment. A chatbot answers customers' questions at any time of day, but it may give wrong answers or fail to understand the customer.

explanation: Two applications, each with a linked benefit or concern.
hints: Give the benefit and the concern in two different applications.

stem: Explain how bias can arise in an AI system and how it can be reduced. [4]

points.description: The training data does not represent all the groups of people or cases
The system learns the patterns of the well-represented groups
It therefore makes more errors for the groups that are under-represented
It can be reduced by collecting more representative data and testing each group separately

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: If the training data does not represent all groups, the system learns the patterns of the well-represented groups and makes more errors for the under-represented ones. This can be reduced by collecting more representative data and testing each group separately.

explanation: Cause, effect, remedy.
hints: Explain the cause, the effect and what could be done.

stem: A hospital in Mutare is considering using AI to help read X-ray images. Discuss whether it should do so. [6]

points.description: A benefit: faster checking of images / helps when specialists are few
A second benefit: can point out areas a doctor might miss
A concern: errors could harm patients / may be less accurate for some patients
A second concern: patients' images are personal data that must be protected
A safeguard: a qualified person makes the final decision / test on local patients
A reasoned conclusion that follows from the points

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Using AI could speed up checking and help where specialists are few, and it can highlight areas that a doctor might miss. However, errors could harm patients, the system may be less accurate for patients unlike those in its training data, and the images are personal data that must be protected. The hospital should use it as support, with a qualified person making every final decision and the system tested on local patients.

explanation: Balanced points and a conclusion.
hints: Two benefits, two concerns and a conclusion.

stem: Discuss the effect of AI on the environment. [3]

points.description: Training and running large AI systems uses a lot of electricity and produces heat that needs cooling
Equipment becomes e-waste / the energy may come from fossil fuels
AI can help the environment, for example by finding crop disease early or reducing waste in supply and power use

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Training and running large AI systems uses a lot of electricity and needs cooling, and the equipment eventually becomes e-waste. AI can also help the environment, for example by detecting crop disease early or reducing waste.

explanation: Costs and benefits.
hints: Mention both energy use and a benefit.

stem:
A crop-disease app was trained on 5000 photographs and tested as shown:

| Crop | Training photographs | Test photographs | Correct | Accuracy |
|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|:-:|
| Maize | 4200 | 150 | 135 | 90% |
| Sorghum | 800 | 50 | 30 | 60% |

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Calculate the accuracy of the app for sorghum, as a percentage.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Calculate the percentage of the training photographs that show sorghum.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Use your answers to suggest why the app is less accurate for sorghum.

points.description: Only 16% of the training photographs were sorghum, so there were few examples to learn from
The app learned maize patterns much better than sorghum patterns

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Only 16% of the training photographs showed sorghum, so the app had few examples to learn from and learned maize better.

parts.label: (d)
parts.stem: State two actions that the developers could take to improve the app for sorghum farmers.

points.description: Collect more photographs of sorghum for training
Test the app on each crop separately / ask sorghum farmers to check the results

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Collect more photographs of sorghum for training, and test the app on each crop separately.

parts.explanation: More representative data and separate tests.

parts.label: (e)
parts.stem: Explain why the overall accuracy of 82.5% could mislead a sorghum farmer.

points.description: The overall figure is dominated by the maize results (150 of 200 photographs)
The farmer would expect better results than the 60% accuracy that applies to sorghum

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: The overall figure is dominated by the maize photographs, so a sorghum farmer would expect better results than the 60% that applies to sorghum.

explanation: Overall accuracy hides poor accuracy on the smaller crop.
hints: Compare the training share with the accuracy.

stem: A bank in Harare introduces a chatbot to answer customers' questions about their accounts.

parts.label: (a)
parts.stem: Give two benefits of the chatbot to the bank or its customers.

points.description: It is available at any time of day
It can answer many customers at once / reduces waiting and cost

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: It is available at any time of day and it can answer many customers at the same time.

parts.label: (b)
parts.stem: Give two concerns about the chatbot.

points.description: It may give a wrong answer or not understand the question
Customers' account details are personal data that must be kept secure / some staff may lose their jobs

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: It may give a wrong answer or fail to understand the customer, and customers' account details are personal data that must be kept secure.

parts.label: (c)
parts.stem: Suggest one way in which the bank could reduce the risk of the chatbot causing harm.

points.description: Let the customer reach a member of staff when the chatbot cannot help
Test the chatbot with customers who speak different languages / protect the data

answerSpec.markingNotes: Example answer: Let customers reach a member of staff when the chatbot cannot help, and test it with customers who speak different languages.

parts.explanation: A human back-up and wide testing.

explanation: A short discussion of a chatbot for a bank.
hints: Give a benefit and a concern for each part.
